title: RuneScape dev apologises after RuneFest debut of an AI-generated six-fingered character: 'That's pretty hard to explain away'
source_used: PC Gamer (full text from the fulltext folder); Kotaku read to corroborate
key_facts: Jagex, the RuneScape developer, held its annual RuneFest in Birmingham over the weekend; in its RuneScape keynote it showed a trailer for its upcoming Dragon Slayer 2 quest.
The trailer featured a player character with six fingers and sneaker-like soles on armoured shoes; posts on social media quickly pointed out what looked like generative AI.

A statement on the 2007scape subreddit from Jagex's Sween said the trailer was taken down while Jagex investigates urgently; it was made by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed GenAI would not be used.
The statement said the sixth finger was 'pretty hard to explain away' and apologised.

Jagex says it does not use GenAI to create its games, artwork or creative assets and will not knowingly allow it to be used on its behalf; this is the second time in quick succession that concerns arose through trusted partners, which points to an issue with its own processes.
Jagex is 'overhauling' its review process and will commission community creators to tell the Dragon Slayer 2 story.
The earlier case, days before, involved a clothing collaboration with 100 Thieves (Kotaku: a collaborative Old School RuneScape T-shirt design; Jagex and 100 Thieves apologised).

Sween said the team 'should have caught these things' and 'can't simply place the blame elsewhere'; Kotaku also reports the takedown and statement, and that some fans are sympathetic while others are not.
quote_evidence: RuneScape developer Jagex descended upon Birmingham (the British one, not the Alabama one) over the weekend with its annual RuneFest.
This trailer was produced by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed that GenAI would not be used.

This is the second time in quick succession that concerns about generative AI have arisen through partners we trusted, and for us that highlights an issue with our own processes which we must address.
why_it_matters_hint: A second case in days of suspected AI-made art reaching players through an outside partner; Jagex admits its own review process failed and says it is being overhauled.
event_date: Trailer shown at RuneFest over the weekend (3-4 Oct 2026); takedown and apology reported on Mon 5 Oct 2026
notes: Confirmed by Jagex's own Reddit statement, quoted alike by PC Gamer and Kotaku, and reported by IGN and games.gg per the Google News listing. The exact time of the statement is not given; all four outlets carry it on 5 Oct 2026, so it is treated as new in the window, with the weekend debut stated in the summary. PC Gamer calls the Jagex author Alec 'Mod Sween' Sween and Kotaku calls him Alex Sween, a social media manager, so the entry names only Jagex.
